forms.detail: Formula C4H6O2 and molar mass 86.0892 (NIST) / 86.09 g/mol (DEA Diversion); CAS 96-48-0 (NIST, read twice). Other names (NIST): γ-butyrolactone, dihydro-2(3H)-furanone, γ-hydroxybutyric acid lactone. DEA: a colourless, oily liquid used as an industrial intermediate and solvent, found in paint removers, cleaners, adhesives and nail polish removers. EUDA: GHB's precursor, sold as a solvent; online suppliers market it as cleaning solvents, multi-purpose removers or chrome polish and wheel cleaners.

Formula C4H10O2 and molar mass 90.1210 (NIST) / 90.12 g/mol (DEA Diversion); CAS 110-63-4 (NIST, read twice). Other names (NIST): butane-1,4-diol, tetramethylene glycol, 1,4-BD. DEA: a colourless, viscous liquid used as an industrial solvent and chemical intermediate; diverted when sold as a cleaner or paint stripper. AIHW describes GBL and 1,4-BD as closely related to GHB.
EUDA: GHB is usually a liquid formulation; DEA: a clear, colourless liquid.
EUDA: rarely a powder, loose or in capsules; DEA: a white powder.
DEA: Xyrem (sodium oxybate), an FDA-approved product distributed through a central pharmacy (United States).
EUDA (European Drug Report 2026): seizures of GHB or its precursor GBL amounted to 34.9 kilograms and 455 litres.
